text.p: The following are the leading stories in the local press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A group of Blantyre women have filed a complaint with the Anti-Corruption Bureau against the country's women lending institution, Womens' World Banking (WWB), for allegedly swindling them out of over three million kwacha ($200,000).
- Police in the Nsanje district of southern Malawi have recovered 12 metric tonnes of maize, meant for flood victims, which went missing in April.

- Malawi Police is arranging for the return of cars stolen from the country and was recovered by Zambian counterparts with assistance from International Police (INTERPOL), police spokesman Willie Chingaru said on Thursday.

- A British chartered accounting firm has been named as one of the three consultants hired to evaluate cabinet functions. They have recommended that Malawi's cabinet be trimmed down to 20 from 26 ministries.

- Anti-Corruption Bureau Director Guilton Chiwaula has been dropped from the list of accused persons in the 137 million kwacha fraud case after the prosecution discovered that he was acting on instructions from one of the accused.
